findings.claim: The brief says that 'the Mœglin–Waldspurger Eisenstein-series inputs ... are planned nowhere and are built here', and it imports nothing from AutomorphicSpectralTheory. This is false. AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1, AS.2 and AS.4 plan the general theory these five items use: convergence of Eisenstein series, constant terms as Weyl sums of intertwining operators, standard and normalized intertwining operators, meromorphic continuation, functional equations, regularity on the unitary axis, and the residual spectrum along cuspidal data. The roadmap names Mœglin–Waldspurger as its proof reference. Accepted extractions of other papers already assign this material there. PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22/28 marks Eisenstein series and intertwining operators of discrete (not only cuspidal) automorphic forms planned at AS.1–AS.2. PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 route 3 sends the Mœglin–Waldspurger normalization of GL × GL intertwining operators ([MW89]) to AS.2. Even on the narrowest reading of AS.1 ('cuspidal data on M'), the rank-one series E_{τ,θ,1} of (4.2) is induced from cuspidal data (|det|^s τ ⊗ θ on the Siegel Levi GL_k × G_0), so its constant term and continuation are AS.1–AS.2 material. Two of the three other routes merged into the same design job (DESIGN-AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartII) import Eisenstein series and intertwining operators from AutomorphicSpectralTheory. The design job therefore receives contradictory instructions, and the Part II would plan this general theory a second time. Also: The route 1 brief says that 'the Mœglin–Waldspurger Eisenstein-series inputs ... are planned nowhere and are built here', and it imports neither AutomorphicSpectralTheory nor AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups. This is false, and as written the Part II would rebuild the general theory of Eisenstein series, which AutomorphicSpectralTheory owns. (a) The rank-one series E_{τ,θ,1} of rev-holomorphy-of-the-rank-one-siegel is an Eisenstein series of cuspidal data (τ ⊗ θ on M_P ≅ GL_k × G_0). Its convergence and its constant term (4.2) are AS.1; the meromorphic continuation of M_0(s) and of the series is AS.2. Yet the item is 'missing' and routed to the Part II. (b) Part (i) of rev-eisenstein-series-regularity-on-the-unitary ([MW95, Theorem VI.2.1(i)], holomorphy on Re(s) = 0) is AS.2's regularity on the unitary axis, which AS.2 plans for cuspidal data. (c) Part (ii) of rev-square-integrability-criterion-and-hermitian-symmetry ([MW95, V.3.13–V.3.16]) rests on the decomposition of L² along cuspidal data and on the residual spectrum. AS.4 owns these, together with the pseudo-Eisenstein prefix that the confirmed finding RT-AREA-automorphic-1/5 adds inside AutomorphicSpectralTheory. (d) The convergence and meromorphic continuation in eisenstein-series ([Lan76, MW95]) are AS.1–AS.2 theory. The accepted PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20/eisenstein-series is also induced from non-cuspidal data, and it is marked planned at AS.1–AS.2. (e) The absolute convergence of Z in global-integral rests on the rapid decay of cusp forms, which AF.3 plans. Only the extensions specific to this paper are new: the series induced from the residual ρ_c(τ); [MW95, Remark IV.3.12] in the form used; Lemma I.4.10; the criterion of §I.4.11; and the Hermitian-symmetry consequence of Remark V.3.6(b).

A later sentence says 'the Langlands classification for G_c and GL_c ... are planned nowhere and are built here'. The import sentence is also wrong for archimedean fields. findings.claim: The proof of Theorem 0.1 must verify one hypothesis of the Converse Theorem: that L(s, Π) converges absolutely in a right half-plane. Nor does it follow from any item. global-integral gives meromorphy of L^S(s, π × τ) through (4.10), not absolute convergence of the Euler product. rev-twisted-euler-products-for-the-converse (i) only passes from L(s, Π) to L(s, Π × τ). What is needed is a uniform bound on the Satake parameters of the unramified, unitary π_ν. Statement: 'Let F be a number field, π an irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A), and S ⊇ S_∞ a finite set of places outside which π is unramified. There is a constant A, depending only on G, such that for every ν ∉ S every eigenvalue of r_G(t_{π_ν}) has absolute value at most q_ν^A. (The spherical function of a unitary unramified representation is positive definite, hence bounded, so by Macdonald's formula the real part of its Satake parameter lies in the convex hull of the Weyl orbit of ρ.) Hence L^S(s, π) = ∏_{ν∉S} det(1 − r_G(t_{π_ν}) q_ν^{−s})^{−1} converges absolutely for Re(s) > A + 1.' Locator: 'arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.4, proof of Theorem 0.1, p. 40 (asserted without reference)'. findings.claim: The proof of Theorem 0.1 opens with 'For the proof we can assume π is unitary'. Everything after that step is for unitary π: Theorem 4.8 assumes it, and so does the construction behind Remark 4.9. But Theorem 0.1, Remark 4.9 and Theorem 4.10 are stated for every cuspidal π. For Sp_c and SO_c every cuspidal π is unitary. For GSpin_c the central character of π, and hence χ_π, can be non-unitary. The reduction needs two facts. (a) π ≅ |Υ_c|^{s_0} π_0 with s_0 real and π_0 unitary cuspidal. (b) T(|Υ_c|^{s_0} π_ν) ≅ |det|^{s_0} T(π_ν) at unramified and archimedean places. Then |det|^{s_0} Π_0 is a weak transfer of π with archimedean component T(π_∞). No item states either fact, and the prerequisites of main and coarse-global contain no such step.
findings.evidence: The paper (arXiv v5, p. 40): 'Let π be a cuspidal representation of G(A). For the proof we can assume π is unitary.' p. 39, Theorem 4.8: 'Assume that π and τ are unitary cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A), resp.' p. 41, Theorem 4.10: 'Let π be a cuspidal representation of G(A) and let Π be a weak functorial transfer of π.' Its proof says 'Thus we may assume by Remark 4.9 ...'. Check of (b): Υ_c has ⟨Υ_c, e_0^∨⟩ = 2 and is trivial on Spin_c, so Υ_c = 2e_0 + e_1 + ... + e_n in X. The weights of the standard representation of Ĝ = GSp_{2n}(C) or GSO_{2n}(C) are e_i^∨ and e_0^∨ − e_i^∨ (1 ≤ i ≤ n). Each pairs to 1 with Υ_c, so r_G ∘ Υ_c is the scalar cocharacter. This agrees with (3.8), p. 16: γ(s, |Υ_c|^{s_0}π × τ, ψ) = γ(s + s_0, π × τ, ψ), which is the Rankin–Selberg γ(s, |det|^{s_0}Π × τ, ψ) when Π is a coarse transfer of π.

findings.claim: Part (i) says that the negative-cone condition of [MW95, §I.4.11], 'with M ≅ GL_k^c', 'reads Σ_{i<=j} Re(e_i) < 0 for 1 <= j <= c'. This reading is right when the roots of A_M in U_{P_{(k^c)}} form a system of type C_c, that is for k ≥ 2 or H = Sp_2c. It is wrong for k = 1 and H = SO_2c or GSpin_2c. There P_{(1^c)} = B_H and the system is of type D_c, with simple roots e_1 − e_2, ..., e_{c−1} − e_c, e_{c−1} + e_c. The condition ⟨Re e, ϖ^∨⟩ < 0 for the fundamental coweights then reads: Σ_{i≤j} Re(e_i) < 0 for j ≤ c − 2, Σ_{i≤c−1} Re(e_i) − Re(e_c) < 0, and Σ_{i≤c} Re(e_i) < 0. Negative partial sums do not give the middle inequality. For c = 2, Re e = (−0.1, −5) has partial sums −0.1 and −5.1, but Re e = 2.45(e_1 − e_2) − 2.55(e_1 + e_2) has a positive coefficient. The case is in the main chain. The Converse Theorem uses k = 1 twists, and for G = SO_c or GSpin_c, H = G_{2c} is of type D. So (i) states a false criterion there. The paper makes the partial-sum check only in the main case and calls k = 1 'similar and simpler'. I computed the exponents of the residue from (4.9) for c ≤ 4, and they do satisfy the type D_c inequalities. So the defect is in the item, not in the paper's conclusion.
findings.evidence: The paper (arXiv v5, p. 36): 'We need to show that for any e = (e_1,...,e_c) ∈ e(s_0,c), i.e., the real part of a cuspidal exponent of E along P_{(k^c)}, Σ_{i=1}^j Re(e_i) < 0 for all 1 ≤ j ≤ c.' p. 38: 'The proof for k = 1 (H = SO_2c or GSpin_2c) is similar and simpler: in identity (4.9) M_1^□(s) is omitted, and P_{(k^c)} = B_H which is normalized by ȷ.' Item statement: 'Suppose the real parts of all its cuspidal exponents lie in the open negative cone; with M ≅ GL_k^c this reads Σ_{i<=j} Re(e_i) < 0 for 1 <= j <= c.' For D_c, ϖ_{c−1}^∨ = (e_1^* + ... + e_{c−1}^* − e_c^*)/2. For k ≥ 2 the roots 2e_i come from ∧² of a GL_k block, which gives type C_c.

findings.claim: No item covers Bernstein's continuation principle in the form of Banks [Ban98]. The appendix cites it as the source of meromorphic continuation (rationality in q^{-s}) of the GL_c × GL_k integrals over p-adic fields for every irreducible π and generic τ. rev-analytic-properties-of-the-gl-c mentions it only inside its statement. No item states it, gives it a status or routes it, and no atlas layer plans it. For ramified π over a p-adic field it is the only source of continuation. The appendix's own continuation argument via multiplicativity is restricted to unramified π or archimedean F. So the existence of γ(s, π × τ, ψ) in (A.3) for ramified π, and the first assertion of Theorem A.2 as gl-multiplicativity states it for all π ∈ Irr(GL_c), depend on it. The main chain, Theorem A.11 for unramified π, does not use it.
findings.evidence: arXiv v5, p. 42: 'We will deduce the meromorphic continuation and continuity (in the restricted setup of representations that are of interest here) using a multiplicativity result ... and we proceed assuming they hold.' p. 50: 'Further assume that either F is non-archimedean and π is unramified ..., or F is archimedean ... Of course over non-archimedean fields the meromorphic continuation already follows from Theorem A.1, the fact that the integral can be made constant, and Bernstein's continuation principle ([Ban98]), for all irreducible representations π and τ such that τ is generic.' gl-multiplicativity states Theorem A.2 for every π ∈ Irr(GL_c) over any F. gl-integral says only 'given meromorphic continuation'. A search of all atlas stage descriptions and all paper items finds no plan for Bernstein's continuation principle; the only mention is in rev-analytic-properties-of-the-gl-c.
findings.fix: Add an item 'Bernstein's continuation principle (Banks's corollary)' (kind theorem, status missing, locator 'Appendix A, p. 50, citing [Ban98]'). Its statement: let F be non-archimedean and V a complex vector space of countable dimension. Suppose a system of linear equations Ξ(s), whose coefficients are polynomials in q^{-s}, q^{s}, has a unique solution for s in a nonempty open set. Then that solution is rational in q^{-s}. Its consequence here: for every π ∈ Irr(GL_c) and generic τ, Z(s, ω, W) and Z*(s, ω, W) are rational in q^{-s}, by Theorem A.1 and the constant choice of data. Route it with the Part II (route 1), and add it to the prerequisites of gl-multiplicativity and gl-integral. In gl-multiplicativity, add: 'over a non-archimedean field with π ramified, the factors exist by [Ban98]'. Add [Ban98] to the extraction's top-level prerequisites.

findings.claim: The paper says 'Dually, e_0 is the similitude character of Ĝ_l' and writes e_0(g) for the similitude of Ĝ: in GO_l(C) and GSp_{l−1}(C), in the dual Levi isomorphism î_M, and in 'det r_{GSpin_c} = e_0^{N/2}'. The extraction copies this ('for GSpin, e_0 is the similitude character of Ĝ'). Under the paper's own convention, the based root datum (X, Δ, X^∨, Δ^∨) has X = X^*(T_G), as used for Υ_l ∈ X and C°_G = e_0^∨(GL_1). The maximal torus of Ĝ then has character lattice X^∨. Its similitude character is the element of X^∨ orthogonal to the coroots Δ of Ĝ, namely e_0^∨. The element e_0 is a cocharacter of T̂, not a character of Ĝ. The sourceIssues do not record this.
findings.evidence: TeX source, §1: 'Dually, $e_0$ is the similitude character of $\Dual{\mathcal{G}}_l$.' The paper (arXiv v5, p. 7) has 'GO_l(C) = {g ∈ GL_l(C) : ᵗg J_{SO_l} g = e_0(g) J_{SO_l}}' and 'î_M(diag(a_1,...,a_d,g′,e_0(g′)a_d^*,...,e_0(g′)a_1^*)) = (a_1,...,a_d,g′)'. On p. 12 it has 'det r_{GSpin_c} = e_0^{N/2}'. Check for GSpin_{2n+1}: the long simple root of Ĝ = GSp_2n(C) is t_n²/λ, and it is 2e_n^∨ − e_0^∨ ∈ Δ^∨, so λ = e_0^∨. Check for GSpin_3 ≅ GL_2, in the coordinates of sourceIssue E3 (e_0 = ε_2, e_1 = ε_1 − ε_2, e_0^∨ = ε_1^∨ + ε_2^∨): the similitude of Ĝ = GL_2(C) is det, which restricts to ε_1^∨ + ε_2^∨ = e_0^∨ on T̂. Here e_0 = ε_2 is the cocharacter z ↦ diag(1, z) of T̂. Also det r_{GSpin_3} = det = (e_0^∨)^{N/2} with N = 2.

findings.claim: The item's argument says 'Theorem 0.1 applies to the G_{c−2l} factor, and the transfer is the corresponding isobaric sum'. Theorem 0.1 is stated only for G_c with c > 1. It does not apply when c − 2l ≤ 1 or when G_{c−2l} = Sp_0, that is, for Sp_0, SO_0, SO_1, GSpin_0 and GSpin_1. Those cases still have an explicit transfer. findings.fix: Restate the argument. By [Lan79b], π is a constituent of Ind(σ_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ σ_d ⊗ π_0), with σ_i cuspidal on GL_{β_i}(A) and π_0 cuspidal on G_{c−2l}(A). findings.claim: For G = SO_2 and G = GSpin_2 (c = 2), Theorem 3.12 and the L-factor of §3.4 are not defined for every π ∈ Irr_rel,a.u.(G). Both groups are tori and have no proper parabolic subgroup. Take G = SO_2 ≅ GL_1, with i_M(diag(x, x^{−1})) = x, and π = |·|^a ∘ i_M with a < 0 real. Then π is unramified, χ_π = 1, so π ∈ Irr_rel,a.u.(SO_2), and π is not tempered. It is not 'essentially tempered' in the paper's sense, since r_0 = 0 is forced for G ≠ GSpin_c. It is not a Langlands quotient σ ⋊ π′ with l > 0, since σ ⋊ π′ = σ ∘ i_M with exponent a_1 > 0. So L(s, π × τ) is undefined, and the step 'write π as the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ as in (3.16)' in the proof of Theorem 3.12 fails. For GSpin_2 = GL_1 × GL_1 the same happens for π = |e_1|^a, a < 0, which has χ_π unitary. The expected factor is L(s, T(π) × τ) = L(s + a, τ)L(s − a, τ). The main theorems are unaffected: Theorem 3.12 is applied in Theorem 4.8 only to local components of unitary cuspidal π, and for these tori those components are unitary, hence tempered. The sourceIssues do not record this. E6 adds l = 0 only for essentially tempered π.
